flashcards.front: How do PagedAttention and Continuous Batching dramatically increase LLM serving throughput?
flashcards.back: Continuous batching schedules requests at each token step instead of waiting for the longest batch sequence to finish, while PagedAttention eliminates >60% KV-cache VRAM fragmentation using non-contiguous memory blocks.

quizzes.scenario: Your gateway limits each user to 60 requests per minute. One user sends 60 prompts a minute, each with 100,000 tokens of context, and saturates the GPU fleet.
quizzes.question: Which change closes this gap?
options: Limit by IP subnet so one office cannot send so many calls
Add a per-user token budget alongside the request limit
Cap the response length while leaving input unlimited
Lower the request limit from 60 to 20 per minute per user
quizzes.explanation: GPU time and KV-cache memory scale with tokens, not requests. Add a tokens-per-minute budget next to the request limit: reserve the estimated tokens when a request starts and refund unused output tokens when the stream ends.
optionExplanations: Subnet limits punish shared offices and still count requests, not tokens.
Correct. Long prompts now cost what they actually consume.
The cost here comes from 100,000-token inputs, which this leaves untouched.
Twenty huge prompts can still saturate GPUs while hurting normal users.
